ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular coil labeled a, b, c, d; the coil rotates around a vertical dashed axis; a large number of crosses in the background indicate that the direction of the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and inward; the coil is connected to an external resistor R through the circuit below, and a voltmeter and an ammeter are also drawn in the circuit. Reasoning: It is known that S=0.05 m^2, N=100, r=1 Ω, R=4 Ω, B=1/π T, ω=100π rad/s. Timing starts from the neutral plane, so at t=0 the magnetic flux is maximum, and the magnetic flux can be written as Φ=NBS cos(ωt). From Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction e=-dΦ/dt, obtain e=NBSω sin(ωt). Substitute the values: NBSω=100×(1/π)×0.05×100π=500, so e=500 sin(100πt). The total resistance of the whole circuit is R_tot=R+r=4+1=5 Ω; the period of one cycle is T=2π/ω=2π/(100π)=0.02 s. The Joule heat produced in each cycle is Q=∫_0^T e^2/R_tot dt=∫_0^T 500^2 sin^2(100πt)/5 dt. The average value of sin^2 in one period is 1/2, so Q=(500^2/5)×(0.02/2)=500 J.

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, the area of the coil is $S=0.05\mathrm{m}^{2}$, with a total of $N=100$ turns. The resistance of the coil is $r=1\Omega$, and the external resistance is $R=4\Omega$. The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B=\frac{1}{\pi}\mathrm{T}$. When the coil rotates at a constant angular velocity of $\omega=100\pi\mathrm{rad/s}$, find:

1. If timing starts when the coil is at the neutral plane, write the expression for the instantaneous value of the induced electromotive force in the coil. Do not add any other content.
2. For each full rotation of the coil, the Joule heat generated in the entire circuit is
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular coil labeled a, b, c, d; the coil rotates around a vertical dashed axis; a large number of crosses in the background indicate that the direction of the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and inward; the coil is connected to an external resistor R through the circuit below, and a voltmeter and an ammeter are also drawn in the circuit. Reasoning: It is known that S=0.05 m^2, N=100, r=1 Ω, R=4 Ω, B=1/π T, ω=100π rad/s. Timing starts from the neutral plane, so at t=0 the magnetic flux is maximum, and the magnetic flux can be written as Φ=NBS cos(ωt). From Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction e=-dΦ/dt, obtain e=NBSω sin(ωt). Substitute the values: NBSω=100×(1/π)×0.05×100π=500, so e=500 sin(100πt). The total resistance of the whole circuit is R_tot=R+r=4+1=5 Ω; the period of one cycle is T=2π/ω=2π/(100π)=0.02 s. The Joule heat produced in each cycle is Q=∫_0^T e^2/R_tot dt=∫_0^T 500^2 sin^2(100πt)/5 dt. The average value of sin^2 in one period is 1/2, so Q=(500^2/5)×(0.02/2)=500 J.
